content.value_statement: Azure Monitor queries can be hard to assemble across logs, metrics, and time ranges. This skill provides focused Python SDK examples for reliable querying.
actual_capabilities: Shows how to install the Azure Monitor Query Python package.
Demonstrates DefaultAzureCredential setup for Azure SDK clients.
Provides LogsQueryClient examples for workspace queries and time ranges.
Provides MetricsQueryClient examples for metrics, aggregations, and dimensions.
Includes batch query, partial result, DataFrame, async client, and Kusto query patterns.
limitations: It is a documentation skill and does not run Azure queries by itself.
It requires Azure credentials, workspace identifiers, and permissions configured outside the skill.
Examples need validation against your Azure tenant, schema, and retention settings.
It does not cover every Azure Monitor Query SDK method or every Kusto pattern.

use_cases.title: Diagnose application incidents
use_cases.description: Use log and metric examples to investigate request failures, exceptions, latency, and resource health.

use_cases.title: Build monitoring notebooks
use_cases.description: Convert query results into DataFrames for exploration, reporting, and recurring operational analysis.

use_cases.title: Learn Azure SDK querying
use_cases.description: Follow concise client examples for authentication, time ranges, batch queries, metrics, and async workflows.

prompt_templates.title: Run a basic log query
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner setup for a Log Analytics workspace query.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the Azure Monitor Query Python skill to show a basic LogsQueryClient workflow for AppRequests over the last hour.

prompt_templates.title: Query resource metrics
prompt_templates.scenario: Create a metrics query for one Azure resource.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to outline a MetricsQueryClient example for CPU and network metrics with a five-minute granularity.

prompt_templates.title: Build batch log checks
prompt_templates.scenario: Compare multiple operational queries in one workflow.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to design a batch query plan for AppRequests and AppExceptions, including partial result handling.

prompt_templates.title: Create observability workflow
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced investigation combining logs, metrics, and analysis patterns.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use this skill to combine Kusto queries, metric aggregations, dimensions, DataFrame conversion, and async clients for a production investigation.

output_examples.input: Ask for a one-hour AppRequests query.
output_examples.output: A Python workflow that authenticates, creates a logs client, queries the workspace, and summarizes request rows by time and result code.

output_examples.input: Ask to inspect CPU and network metrics for an Azure resource.
output_examples.output: A metrics query plan that selects metric names, time range, granularity, and aggregation choices for the requested resource.

output_examples.input: Ask for batch troubleshooting across requests and exceptions.
output: Recommended batch queries for request and exception tables.
Partial result handling guidance for incomplete or failed responses.
A short explanation of how to review the returned tables.

best_practices: Confirm workspace IDs and resource URIs before running examples.
Use narrow time ranges and filters before expanding queries.
Handle partial results and failures before automating reports.
anti_patterns: Do not paste production secrets into prompts or sample code.
Do not run broad tenant-wide queries without cost and access review.
Do not treat sample Kusto as validated for every schema.

faq.question: Does this skill run Azure queries automatically?
faq.answer: No. It provides documentation and examples that a user can adapt and run in their own environment.

faq.question: Which Azure SDK does it cover?
faq.answer: It covers the Azure Monitor Query SDK for Python, including logs and metrics clients.

faq.question: Does it require Azure credentials?
faq.answer: Yes. The examples assume Azure identity configuration and permissions are already available.

faq.question: Can it help write Kusto queries?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes common Kusto examples for requests, exceptions, slow requests, and top errors.

faq.question: Can it help with pandas analysis?
faq.answer: Yes. It shows how query results can be converted into a DataFrame for analysis.

faq.question: How should I handle sensitive monitoring data?
faq.answer: Avoid sharing secrets or sensitive query output. Review results before adding them to prompts, tickets, or reports.
